Downstream review engines can only ever act on the ~42% who clear this gate, so lifting the gate raises the ceiling for all of them at once.

PR #8 rebuilt the layout/hierarchy -> flat (44.5% -> 39.0%). 2026-07-23 reworded two lines of opening voice -> shipped, unmeasurable, pending. Plus INFRA-only instrumentation (07-20, 07-22) and two OWNER-REJECTED ideas (discount-first; printed-% gap). Per the rules a single failed/shipped mechanism fences only that mechanism - the distrust, hidden-emotional-hook, single-value, no-reason-now and felt-cost causes have never been attacked here. Today's change is the third real attempt: surfacing the already-fetched character image (imagery), a distinct mechanism.
choice_reasoning.what_history_suggests: Pattern across all changes: the one thing that MOVED this funnel was a concrete mechanism change with a real reason (2026-06-16 email-first delivery + value-prop hero: +14pts in-app, held 3 weeks). The things that did NOTHING were a generic presentation reshuffle (PR #8) and word-only tweaks. That argues for a specific, mechanism-driven change with a tangible lever - here, surfacing a real IMAGE that already exists but is hidden - over another copy pass or another vague reshuffle.

Preview/share review asks feed reviews directly but are tiny in absolute volume (3/21 over 30d) and already reworked once with no effect. The Klaviyo reminder emails are out of this repo's scope. The email gate is bigger, upstream of both other review engines, and the least-worked by distinct mechanism.

change.title: Show the crochet friend on the claim screen instead of hiding it
change.targets: Claim page: landed -> gave email (first-paint engagement of the ~58-61% who currently never engage the email field)
change.expected_effect: A few points of extra email capture at best (well inside the noise floor at ~150 landers/fortnight), by earning first-paint engagement from a slice of the ~58% who currently never touch the field. Directionally lifts every downstream review path since all of them start at this gate.
change.why_it_helps: When someone scans the code on a handmade gift they came because they loved the gift - but the claim screen led with a coupon and an email box and never actually showed the gift. This puts a warm photo of their exact crochet friend right at the top, so the screen matches why they scanned before it asks for anything.
changes_in_plain_words: The claim screen now shows a round, gold-framed photo of the customer's actual crochet character (with its name) right under the 'Hope it made you smile' line, above the rewards and the email box.
That photo was already being loaded on every visit but was switched off in the code, so the screen about a handmade gift was hiding the gift - this simply turns it on.
If a product doesn't have a character photo, nothing extra shows - the screen looks exactly as it does today, with no empty space or broken image.
Nothing else changed: same 30% off, same free-video offer, same email box and 'Send Me My Code' button, same video lower down.

previews.label: the claim screen (potato) - what a customer sees after scanning
the claim screen (cupcake) - a second product, to show it works across characters

change.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: The gate is an exchange: the visitor hands over an email to get the 30% code and the free video. Converters accept that price because the reward feels real and worth it in the moment. Non-converters, at first paint, are shown a coupon and a form with no emotional anchor to the gift they already love - so the perceived worth of the trade is set by a marketing-form impression rather than by the handmade character that motivated the scan. Raising the felt worth of the page at first paint (showing their friend) is meant to move more people to accept the SAME exchange - it does NOT touch the price (email still required) or what is delivered.
what_would_have_to_be_true: A non-trivial share of the ~58% who never engage are leaving because the first-paint impression fails to connect emotionally, not purely because they never wanted a next-order discount.

The scanning SKUs resolve to a video character so characterImage is non-null and a real portrait renders (top SKUs PTT-GREEN1/FRIENDFUN/CPCK1 map to characters; products with no character keep today's behaviour - the container stays hidden and renders nothing).
A single premium 120px portrait under the kicker reads as warmth/legitimacy, not as clutter that pushes the reward and CTA meaningfully down.
change.second_order_effects: The same character already autoplays as a video preview at the BOTTOM of the page; adding a still portrait at the top creates mild repetition, but the two do different jobs (identity/emotional anchor at first paint vs 'here's what you'll create' tease below the fold that non-engagers never scroll to) and the top placement is where the loss occurs. The image is ALREADY downloaded on load (imgEl.src is set regardless of display), so un-hiding adds zero network bytes - only a decode/paint - so LCP/latency risk is negligible. It pushes the reward list and form down by one compact element; on mobile the kicker+portrait+reward-intro still sit at/near the top of the first viewport (verified in the AFTER screenshots). No gate, reward, delivery path, or promise is touched, so there is no downstream review cost.
change.strongest_case_against: A sceptic would say: the 61% who never type may simply not want a next-order discount (a ceiling no portrait moves), and the character is not truly 'invisible' - the same character autoplays as a video lower down - so this just adds a portrait that shoves the actual reward and CTA further from the top, delaying the ask for the people who WOULD have converted. My answer: (1) the image is already fetched, so there is no added latency, and a 120px portrait is compact - the reward list and form remain immediately below, not materially displaced (the AFTER screenshots confirm the form still sits near the top of the first mobile viewport); (2) the bottom video sits below the fold precisely where non-engagers never scroll, so it does no first-paint work - the whole point is to put the friend where first paint actually is; (3) the ceiling risk is real and acknowledged, which is exactly why this is labelled measurable:false and shipped as a cheap, reversible bet rather than a claimed win - and even under the sceptic's worst case it corrects a genuine defect (a handmade-gift page that hides the gift). If the 2026-08-05 split shows the loss is mostly a discount-ceiling, the next swing pivots to the discount-indifferent segment (e.g. the video co-hero angle).

tradeoff.gained: A warm, on-brand first-paint impression that reconnects the box's promise to the page and gives first-paint non-engagers a reason to look twice before deciding - aimed at the largest, highest-value, least-worked leak.
tradeoff.risked: Negligible measurable downside: no gate, reward, delivery, or promise changes, so the review paths it feeds (in_app thankyou 16/21 and email_redirect 2/21 over 30d) are untouched - this cannot reduce email capture the way the owner-rejected discount-first idea would. The only real risks are null effect (the loss is a discount-ceiling the image can't move) or minor visual clutter; both are fully reversible by re-adding the hidden class default.
unverified_assumptions: That a non-trivial share of the ~58% who never engage the field are leaving for emotional-disconnect reasons rather than a discount-ceiling the image cannot move (the session-replay metadata evidences WHERE the loss sits - first paint - but not WHY; the 2026-08-05 split will separate never-engaged from engaged-declined, though not emotional-disconnect from ceiling).

change.differs_from_past_attempt: PR #8 (spent ground) was a generic full-page layout/hierarchy REBUILD of existing elements that never surfaced this hidden image - a different mechanism (structure vs imagery). The 2026-07-23 opening-voice change reworded two LINES of copy - words, not imagery. This surfaces an already-fetched IMAGE. Neither owner rejection applies: this never hands the discount code over before the email (discount-first, rejected 2026-07-20) and never references or compares to the printed percentage (printed-% gap, rejected 2026-07-19). It is a specific, mechanism-driven imagery change, not PR #8's vague reshuffle - and it matches the pattern that actually moved the funnel (the 2026-06-16 value-prop hero: imagery + reason).

change.commit_message: feat(claim): surface the fetched crochet-character portrait as a first-paint hero

pr_body:
## What this does

When someone scans the QR code on a handmade crochet gift, they land on the claim screen. Today that screen opens with a coupon and an email box - and never actually shows the gift, even though a photo of the exact crochet character is already being downloaded on every visit. It was simply switched off in the code (`display:none`). This change turns it on: a round, gold-framed portrait of the customer's own crochet friend (with its product name) now appears right under the warm 'Hope it made you smile' line, above the rewards and the email box. If a product has no character photo, nothing extra shows and the screen looks exactly as it does today.

**See the attached BEFORE / AFTER photos of the claim screen (potato and cupcake).**

## Verdict on the last change (the warm opening-voice reword, shipped 2026-07-23)

**Not yet measurable - and NOT claimable as a win.** It shipped the same day the measurement window ends, so there is essentially no post-change traffic yet. The email-capture numbers this window vs the prior window are flat and inside the noise:

- This window: 42.2% captured (65 of 154). Prior window: 39.8% (64 of 161).
- `significance.mjs 64 161 65 154` -> +2.5 points, p = 0.658, **NOT SIGNIFICANT** (these sample sizes could only detect a swing of ~16 points or more).

That entry stays 'pending' and re-measures ~2026-08-05. No number here is statistically solid enough to call a result.

## The leaks, ranked

1. **The claim-page email gate (landed -> gave email).** ~58% of scanners never give an email (65 of 154 captured this window; 64 of 161 prior - flat, p=0.66). It's the biggest single drop by headcount, sits at the very top so it multiplies everything after it, and it's the only door to the in-app thank-you screen that produces **76% (16 of 21) of all review clicks** over 30 days. Highest value to reviews, least-worked. **This is what we're fixing.**
2. **In-app: arrived -> started a video** (~38%, 32 of 85). High value, but it was worked on twice in the last five weeks and one of those reads isn't in yet - touching it now would muddy that measurement.
3. **Preview / share review asks** (~0 clicks despite real traffic; 3 of 21 over 30d). Real but tiny, and already reworked once with no effect.

## Why we picked the email gate, and this fix

Every path that produces a review starts with an email, so lifting this gate raises the ceiling for all of them. We looked at session recordings for all 31 claim sessions in the window: **61% (19 of 31) never typed a single key**, and only 12 of 31 typed at all. So people are leaving at first sight of the screen, before they ever touch the email box - which means the fix belongs at first impression, not at the form. The single strongest lever for a first impression is a real image, and there was one sitting fetched-but-hidden in the code: the customer's own crochet character. Showing it reconnects why they scanned (they loved the handmade gift) with what the screen asks - without changing the deal at all.

## Honest limits

We can see *where* people leave (first paint) but not *why*. Some of that 58% may simply not want a next-order discount - a ceiling no photo can move. That's why this is shipped as a small, reversible bet and is **labelled unmeasurable by design**: at ~150 visitors a fortnight, a few points of change can't be told apart from luck (you'd need ~6,000 per window). It will never be called a win without a statistically significant result. Even in the worst case it fixes a real defect - a page about a handmade gift that was hiding the gift.

## What did NOT change

Same 30% off, same free personalized video, same email box, same 'Send Me My Code' button, same video preview lower down. No change to how the discount or video is delivered. The photo was already downloaded on load, so this adds zero extra loading time. It's different from the past claim-page rebuild (PR #8, which reshuffled existing elements and did nothing) - this surfaces a new piece of content (imagery), matching the one change that actually moved this review journey (the June value-prop hero). It does not touch either owner-rejected idea (no code shown before the email; no mention of the printed discount percentage).

## How it was verified

Booted the app locally, loaded the claim screen -> 200 with the new code present and the old hidden setting gone. Drove the real page in a browser: a product with a character showed the gold-framed portrait as intended above the rewards and form, everything else unchanged; a product with no character showed nothing extra with the layout intact. Rendered mobile BEFORE (live site) / AFTER (local) photos for two products. Cleaned up the two test rows the screenshots created.

## What to re-measure, and when

~2026-08-05 (needs ~2 weeks of data on/after the 07-22 instrument fix). Compare `page_viewed -> email_field_engaged` (did they engage the box at all?) and `email_field_engaged -> email_entered` (of those who engaged, who submitted?), plus the PostHog claim-capture rate, then run the significance test. That split tells us how much of the loss is 'never engaged' vs 'engaged then declined' and points the next swing. Expect it to likely stay inside the noise floor either way at this traffic.
telegram_summary:
Last change (warm opening line on the claim screen, 07-23): NOT YET MEASURABLE - shipped the day the window closed; capture is flat 39.8%->42.2% (p=0.66, noise). Not a claimed win.

Top leak: the claim screen email step - ~58% who scan never enter an email, and it's the only door to the review screen that drives 76% of reviews.

What I did: the claim screen was hiding a photo of the customer's own crochet character it already loads. I turned it on - a round gold-framed portrait now sits under 'Hope it made you smile', above the rewards and email box. Nothing else changed. See BEFORE/AFTER photos. Small reversible bet; re-measure ~Aug 5.
